newsitem.title: USA: GM to idle Missouri van plant for one week.
newsitem.headline: GM to idle Missouri van plant for one week.

text.p: General Motors Corp. plans to idle its full-size van assembly plant in Wentzville, Mo., the week of April 21, affecting about 1,600 workers, union officials said Tuesday.
United Auto Workers officials added that GM also has scheduled two weeks of down-time at the plant in July, in addition to the regular two-week summer shutdown the automaker takes in July.
GM spokesman Tom Klipstine declined to confirm the downtime schedules, saying GM has a policy of not releasing production schedules until the week before they are to take effect.
The Wentzville plant is the only GM facility that makes the Chevrolet Express, Chevy Van and GMC Savana full-size vans, used primarily by commercial and conversion-van customers.
Through March of this year, sales of the Chevy Van were down 4.8 percent; Express sales were up 6.5 percent; and Savana sales were down 3.6 percent.
Al Moellenhoff, spokesman for the plant, told the St. Louis Post-Dispatch the shutdown was "volume-related."

The downtime at Wentzville did not affect GM's latest forecast for second quarter North American production, which remains at 1,550,000 cars and trucks -- 1,000 units higher than the second quarter of 1996. The forecast, released Tuesday, is unchanged from estimates made a month ago.

GM said during the first quarter, it built 1,442,000 vehicles in the United States, Canada and Mexico, an 18.3 percent increase over the 1,219,000 vehicles built in the strike-weakened year-ago period.

GM endured a 17-day strike at two brake plants in Dayton, Ohio in March 1996, which paralyzed nearly all of the automaker's 29 North American assembly plants and cost the automaker $900 million in lost profits.
GM's March 1997 North American production rose 71 percent over March 1996 to a total of 465,000 cars and trucks.

GM also said the 1997 first quarter production total of represents an increase of 4,000 units over forecasts released a month ago. GM increased car production by 9,000 units over the prior estimates, while cutting truck production by 5,000 units.

The automaker last month suffered a nearly two week strike at its Fort Wayne, Ind., full-size pickup truck plant. United Auto Workers members struck a GM car plant in Oklahoma City early on Saturday in a walkout that will affect second quarter production.
